sources.label: VENDOR

notes: Fits 'buy this, final price <= X' and post-negotiation capture after delivery. UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 s.15: the mandate is registered only after AFA (15.2); the remitter bank posts success only after blocking the funds and bears liability if they do not remain blocked (15.3); the remitter bank and payer PSP validate the digital signature and parameters at execution (15.4); execution is only up to the authorised amount and a partial execution unblocks the rest (15.5); post-debit SMS and notification for create, update, revoke and debit (15.7); the block period for the Bima-ASBA use case is at most 14 days (15.9). The circular has no pre-debit notice for OTM, and the scope of the E-mandate Framework 2026 para 2 (recurring) for OTM is not confirmed (Q-03). The limits stay vendor-sourced. RBI layer: no RBI exemption basis for the debit of an OTM block was found (not verified as of 18-10-2026; asked of RBI under AJD-37).

binding.open_requires: One block at a time per merchant per mobile number. An open mandate names the block's payee seller (payee.vpa and payee.bpp_id); a block payable to the buyer app does not back human-not-present payment. NPCI OC 200 item 3 and para (d) put all necessary validation at block creation; OC 228 acquirer item 5(c) adds the issuer's responsibility to validate every debit. Neither text says whether a fresh authentication factor is taken at each debit (reading, as of 18-10-2026; Q-88).

notes: NPCI UPI OC 228 (08-10-2025) and the UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 para 16.1 extend Reserve Pay to all UPI-permitted sources of funds, naming savings, current and overdraft accounts, RuPay credit cards and pre-sanctioned credit lines; the extant pricing of RuPay credit cards and credit lines on UPI applies to executed debits. funding stays debit for this descriptor: a block on a RuPay credit card or a credit line is a credit-funded leg (funding credit, in.upi.rupay_cc or in.upi.credit_line), which the PSP attestation states and which needs credit_funding_allowed. Acquirer eligibility: OC 228 enables Reserve Pay to begin with only for 'online verified merchants with low ticket and high frequency transactions'. One mobile number may hold only one block at a time for a particular merchant (OC 228 Issuer Banks para 4; Consolidated Circular para 16.4); no NPCI text caps blocks per user across merchants. A block is not a guarantee of payment. A timeout on a debit is a decline, reversed in real time and not settled; for timeouts only, acquiring entities may retry at most 3 times in 24 hours (OC 228 Acquiring entities para 3). The payer is notified of block creation, modification, debit, revoke and expiry (OC 228 Issuer Banks para 2; Consolidated Circular para 16.11); no NPCI text found states whether a pre-debit notice applies (Q-03). The payee PSP and the UPI app must give the user a facility to revoke the block (Consolidated Circular para 16.10); the merchant gives the facility to modify its amount or validity (para 16.9). No public NPCI list of the issuers that support Reserve Pay was found as of 17-10-2026 (an absence finding; Q-04). NPCI product page: block set up with UPI PIN; unused money is released on expiry or cancellation. Deemed debit, by date and side: a timeout on the debit with the issuer or payer PSP is a decline, reversed in real time and not deemed (OC 228, 08-10-2025, Acquiring entities para 3); a credit-side timeout after a successful debit is deemed (OC 200, 31-07-2024, para (d); Consolidated Circular para 32.3) and follows TAT row 4(b) of RBI/2019-20/67. The scope of deemed debit after OC 228 is not public (OC 88/2020-21 and OC 128/2021-22 are member-only; not verified as of 18-10-2026; AJD-26). RBI layer: no RBI exemption basis for the later debits of a block was found; the Authentication Directions Annexure-1 lists no SBMD item (not verified as of 18-10-2026; asked of RBI under AJD-37). The afa.verification grade covers the NPCI text only.

name.en-IN: Gift PPI (open or semi-closed gift card)

binding.open_requires: Balance is the cap. No reload, no cash-out. A gift PPI is accepted only by a seller that has a contract with the issuer to accept it (PPI MD para 2.6), and by any merchant only where the issuer offers interoperability, which is its option (PPI MD para 11.4.3), so the seller's acceptance is checked before the rung is ranked. Open only when the PSP attestation states that the gift code vault is on the principal's side (the Trusted Surface or the payer PSP); otherwise the Mandate Manager refuses issuance.
